sources.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories

articles.author: Kristin Wright
articles.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said he believes the U.S. government is behind his military's loss of normal access to the key satellite communications service used by the Ukrainian military.
articles.title: Ukraine and the U.S. are at odds over Starshield. Here's what to know

articles.author: Scott Detrow
articles.description: One of NPR's most gifted storytellers, his soft voice and vivid writing helped define the network's sound for a generation of Americans.
articles.title: Noah Adams, longtime host of NPR's All Things Considered, has died

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Pope Leo XIV thanked thousands of faithful in St. Peter's Square on Sunday for their prayers while he was hospitalized, and said he plans to gradually return to his usual duties.
articles.title: Pope Leo says he will gradually resume duties after cancer surgery

articles.author: Samantha Balaban
articles.description: As the American Girl doll company celebrates its 40th anniversary, Samantha has turned 25 — and is the subject of a new historical fiction novel by author Fiona Davis.
articles.title: 'From socialite to shopgirl': American Girl Samantha gets a new story

articles.author: Claudia Grisales
articles.description: Rep. María Elvira Salazar filmed an ad warning the president that he's "gone too far" on immigration. It reflected concern among some Republicans that their gains with Latino voters could be at risk.
articles.title: With an ad aimed at Trump, this Republican exposed GOP angst about Latino voters

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney described the incident as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's military on domestic soil.
articles.title: Carney says 4 service members killed and dozens injured in fire at Alberta military base

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Police arrested at least 1,800 people across France after violent groups clashed with officers and looted shops during nationwide demonstrations that drew hundreds of thousands of people.
articles.title: France's Macron vows to hold accountable those who 'sought to bring down the Republic'

articles.author: Willem Marx
articles.description: The Pope left Rome's Gemelli Hospital Saturday, days after surgery for lung cancer removed the lower lobe of his right lung. He is currently scheduled to travel to Latin America in November.
articles.title: Pope Leo XIV leaves hospital days after lung cancer surgery

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Zelenskyy described the move as unfortunate, adding it would encourage Russia to continue its assault. Trump told Congress that the pause was in the national interest but gave no further details.
articles.title: Zelenskyy urges support for new US sanctions on Russia after Trump puts them on hold

articles.author: Kate Bartlett
articles.description:
More than three decades after the end of apartheid, families of victims of some of the worst crimes of South Africa's past
are still fighting for justice. As survivors and perpetrators grow older, a new wave of legal efforts is seeking truth, accountability and reparations before it's too late.
articles.title: Decades after apartheid, South Africans seek justice for crimes of the past

articles.author: Josh Butler and Sarah Basford Canales
articles.description:
The new Greens leader says it is his understanding the West Australian senator ‘agreed’ to take leave from the party room
Greens leader David Shoebridge has said it was his understanding Jordon Steele-John agreed to take leave from parliament while misconduct allegations against him are investigated, and that it’s “appropriate” that he does so, despite the Western Australian senator saying overnight that he was not on leave and had never agreed to stay away from parliament.
Steele-John released a lengthy, explosive statement on Sunday night claiming Shoebridge pressured him to take leave after complaints about his conduct were made public last week, and accused an internal faction within the Greens of playing “nasty political games”. He has denied any allegations of misconduct.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: David Shoebridge responds to Jordon Steele-John’s explosive statement as Greens hold emergency meeting

articles.author: Lauren Cochrane
articles.description:
Backlash against content creators includes restricted hours for filming and even outright bans
Stand in any vaguely photogenic spot these days on holiday and the chances are you will come across people posing with raised phones and even ring lights. Some may be influencers with huge audiences on social media, others just overkeen Instagram users. With hotels and beauty spots now so overrun, however, bans on photography are coming into place.
The five-star Hotel du Cap-Eden-Roc in Antibes, known for its glamorous clientele, views of the Côte d’Azur and a stunning infinity pool, has brought in rules against photoshoots: no longer allowed without prior permission.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘No influencers’: the hotels, restaurants and beauty spots restricting photoshoots

articles.author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
articles.description:
McClelland, who served in the Rudd government, named as boss of National Anti-Corruption Commission after Paul Brereton quit in May

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Former Labor attorney general and federal court judge Robert McClelland has been named as the new boss of the National Anti-Corruption Commission.
McClelland was the country’s top law officer in the Rudd government, serving from 2007 until 2011. After leaving parliament in 2013, he has served as the deputy chief justice of the federal circuit and family court of Australia since 2018, after being appointed to the court by the former Coalition government in 2015.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Former Labor attorney general turned judge Robert McClelland named new anti-corruption boss

articles.author: Tess Ikonomou
articles.description:
One Nation leader said Tasmanian senator should ‘get over it’ and claimed the cartoon was ‘satirical’ 

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Anthony Albanese has praised the courage of Jacqui Lambie in speaking out about her struggles with vaginal prolapse, as politicians from across the spectrum condemn a One Nation cartoon.
The latest cartoon, part of Pauline Hanson’s Please Explain series, depicts the army veteran as saying “I can’t laugh because of my prolapsed vagina,” before adding a crude sound effect ridiculing the health condition.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: PM, Coalition and crossbench support Jacqui Lambie after Pauline Hanson cartoon mocked vaginal prolapse

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Accused asked fellow police officer how law enforcement would respond to reports of gunshots days before alleged murders, court hears

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon allegedly told a friend “I love you’” and “not everything in the news is true” a month after he was arrested over a double murder, a court has heard.
Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting Sydney couple Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon told officer friend ‘I love you’ and ‘not everything in the news is true’ after arrest, court told

articles.author: Jordyn Beazley
articles.description:
Amid police brutality allegations, inquiry hears protesters against visit of Israeli president were ‘largely peaceful’

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

An inquiry into a Sydney rally against the Israeli president’s visit has so far found protesters were “largely peaceful” and there is “limited evidence of physical violence on the part of the protesters”.
The Law Enforcement Conduct Commission (Lecc) kicked off its inquiry into the February protest at Sydney’s town hall against the visit of Isaac Herzog on Monday, outlining a number of issues it is examining, including police use of OC spray and “police boasting about gratuitous force”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Limited evidence’ of protester violence at Sydney demonstration against Israeli president Isaac Herzog visit

articles.author: Sanya Mansoor
articles.description:
‘Meta owes us an explanation,’ group says as organizers fear censorship after account goes dark for several hours
The coalition leaders behind nationwide pro-democracy protests that have drawn millions of Americans to the streets in recent years were frustrated when its Instagram account was temporarily shut down during its latest demonstration on Saturday.
The No Kings movement’s account went dark for several hours while protests focused on increasing early voter turnout were underway, sparking censorship fears.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Outrage after Meta suspends No Kings Instagram account during protests

articles.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto, Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Prime minister Mark Carney describes blaze as ‘one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime’
Four people have been killed and dozens more seriously injured after a “violent, fast-moving” fire tore through one of Canada’s busiest military training bases in Alberta, the country’s prime minister said on Sunday.
Mark Carney called the incident “one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Four people killed in ‘violent, fast-moving’ fire at Canadian military base

articles.author: José Olivares and Sanya Mansoor in New York
articles.description:
Ex-president urges Americans to defend congresswoman, saying ‘there’s no reason to believe it will stop with her’
Former US president Barack Obama condemned comments by Donald Trump’s “border czar” that the Republican presidential administration could “of course” strip Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar of her citizenship and deport her.
Obama wrote Sunday morning, on X, that “the full weight of the federal government is being brought down on a law-abiding elected official because she has dared to criticize the president.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Obama condemns comments by ‘border czar’ that Ilhan Omar could ‘of course’ be denaturalized

articles.author: José Olivares
articles.description:
Report reveals that a shady mobster-turned-informant may have been involved in helping cover up murder
An in-depth investigation by the New York Times is raising further questions about the high-profile OJ Simpson case, in which the former football player was accused in the 1990s of killing his ex-wife – and whether a shady mobster-turned-informant may have been involved in helping cover up the murder.
The Times’s investigation revealed that California prosecutors were unable to fully investigate whether Simpson, who was accused but not convicted of his ex-wife’s murder, may have had an accomplice at the scene of the crime.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Times’s investigation adds more intrigue to infamous OJ Simpson case

articles.author: Jasper Jolly
articles.description:
Premium paid over French counterparts has risen to almost £30 a megawatt hour, analysis by lobby group finds
British steelmakers have been pushed further behind European rivals on electricity costs after the US-Israeli war on Iran caused a surge in global gas prices.
The premium paid by the British industry over its French counterpart has risen to almost £30 a megawatt hour (MWh), its highest level in three years, according to analysis by the lobby group UK Steel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Electricity costs put UK steelmakers in worst position in three years against EU rivals

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Passengers urged to ‘share the carriage, not the noise’ as guidance sets out £100 penalties for nuisance behaviour
Andy Burnham has announced a crackdown on “headphone dodgers” who play loud music on public transport, as he extends his promise to give voters “breathing space” in the confines of a train carriage.
The prime minister will unveil a campaign against nuisance behaviour on public transport on Monday, alongside guidance allowing local transport authorities to levy fines of up to £100 for non-compliance.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham launches campaign against ‘headphone dodgers’ on public transport

articles.author: Tom Perkins
articles.description:
Agency changes wording on website as Texas-based firm continues manufacture of plastic container barriers
The Environmental Protection Agency has quietly backtracked on a claim that the US has phased out two of the most dangerous Pfas compounds – Pfoa and Pfos.
The EPA has found that virtually no level of exposure to either in drinking water is safe, and the International Agency for Research on Cancer classifies Pfoa as “carcinogenic to humans” and Pfos as “possibly carcinogenic”. Still, the EPA is allowing Houston-based Inhance to produce containers from which Pfoa has been found to leach at high levels into the containers’ contents. The company makes up to 200m barriers annually for plastic containers used across the US economy.
This article was amended on 18 October 2026 to correct Patricia van Ee’s title, and the story previously stated that Inhance manufactures plastic containers. They make the containers’ barriers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EPA quietly backtracks on claims US has phased out toxic Pfas compounds

articles.author: Press Association
articles.description:
Family post emotional statements to Instagram a month after their son and brother died at a rehab facility
Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber have said they are “beyond heartbroken” in a tribute to their “sweet beautiful” son, Presley.
Their eldest child died aged 27 at a rehab facility on 20 September, according to Los Angeles county medical examiner records. The cause of his death has not been disclosed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We are beyond heartbroken’: Cindy Crawford, Rande and Kaia Gerber share tributes to Presley

articles.author: Hanad Ahmed
articles.description:
Antibody patterns in the blood may help doctors identify people at risk so they can be treated earlier, research shows
Patterns of antibodies in people’s blood could predict the onset of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) a decade before diagnosis, according to research that raises hopes for catching the condition early.
Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis, the two main forms of IBD, are typically treated only after symptoms appear, when the gut has already been damaged. But scientists found that the immune system sends warning signals up to a decade before diagnosis, paving the way for potentially earlier detection and even prevention.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Warning signs could predict inflammatory bowel disease a decade before diagnosis

articles.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
articles.description:
Ministers, officials and police under pressure over response to protests as government holds crisis talks amid ‘colossal failure of the state’
The French president, Emmanuel Macron, has criticised “unbridled violence” after one of the most violent days of unrest in years left public buildings burned, hundreds of shops destroyed and looted and at least 2,400 people arrested in cities across the country.
“Watching these images, we have all asked ourselves how could French people do this to France?” he said in a televised address.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Macron criticises ‘unbridled violence’ after days of unrest and 2,400 arrests across France

articles.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem
articles.description:
New video footage of Israeli settler assault on European delegation as Netanyahu attempts to raise doubt
Hours after Israeli militants attacked a delegation of European diplomats, French clerics and a visiting mayor in the occupied West Bank, Israel’s leader, Benjamin Netanyahu, responded by questioning the delegation’s account of the assault.
“Serious accusations require serious evidence” was the all-caps headline of a social media post from the office of the prime minister. As news of the attack spread globally there was no pledge to find those accountable and bring them to justice.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Guardian reporter filmed masked militants seconds before West Bank attack on French mayor

articles.author: Anna Bawden and Kiran Stacey
articles.description:
Exclusive: Former health secretary says upfront investment in support is needed ‘if we are going to end the Neet crisis’
Ministers should cut welfare spending to fund more employment support if it wants to end the youth Neet crisis, the author of a government-led review has said.
Alan Milburn, the Tony Blair-era health secretary, told the Guardian he believed ministers should reduce benefits payments to help pay for more employment support, opening a potentially contentious debate within the Labour party over welfare cuts.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cut benefits to fund work support for young people, says Neet review author Alan Milburn

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll senior correspondent
articles.description:
UK home secretary’s meeting comes after PM said he wanted to rejoin European law enforcement databases
The UK home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, will meet the EU’s home affairs commissioner on Monday for further talks just days after Andy Burnham said he wanted to rejoin European law enforcement databases from which the UK has been locked out of since Brexit.
According to the European Commission, they will discuss “migration, border management, law enforcement cooperation and counter-terrorism”, with the latest Frontex data published on Monday showing a 43% decline in small boats crossing the Channel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Shabana Mahmood to hold talks with EU over law enforcement cooperation

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Green leader in England and Wales calls ‘debates about words’ unhelpful and denies recent motion was controversial
Zack Polanski has said Zionism in its current form is racist, that no country has a right to exist, and that the Green party motion on the issue was not controversial.
The leader of the Green party in England and Wales gave an unapologetic interview to the BBC on Sunday two weeks after his party approved a motion equating Zionism with racism.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Zack Polanski says application of Zionism is racist and no state has right to exist

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Capt Smit Machchhar said he screamed for help as he reached to open the cockpit door on flight FZ1073
The captain of a flydubai flight who was attacked by a co-pilot who intended to crash the plane has described ⁠blocking axe blows to his head and screaming for help as he reached to open the cockpit door.
Capt Smit ⁠Machchhar has been hailed ⁠as a ​hero for his role in averting disaster on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv last month, helping to thwart what the UAE ⁠attorney general has said was an attempted suicide attack by the co-pilot who had intended to crash the plane into Ben Gurion airport.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Flydubai captain describes blocking axe blows as co-pilot attacked him

articles.author: Sam Jones and agencies
articles.description:
Mike Huckabee calls for arrest and prosecution of those responsible as Heidi Levine, 63, recovers in hospital in Israel
The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, has denounced the settler attack that left the Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine badly beaten and needing surgery as a “despicable act of terror” and called for the arrest and prosecution of those responsible.
Levine, 63, an award-winning journalist who lives in Israel, was set upon last Friday by masked Israeli settlers who used clubs and other weapons to attack Palestinian people attempting to harvest their olives in occupied West Bank towns.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US ambassador to Israel calls West Bank settler attack on American photojournalist ‘terror’

articles.author: Andrew Roth in Kyiv and Sam Jones
articles.description:
Two people killed and at least 17 injured as Russia and Ukraine continue to trade strikes on power infrastructure
Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Sunday thanked the Trump administration for resuming intelligence sharing between the two countries, but maintained the US had intentionally throttled its Starlink satellite internet access so that Donald Trump could send a “message” in his ongoing feud with the Ukrainian president.
In an interview on NBC, Zelenskyy said the US had “unblocked” intelligence on impending Russian ballistic missile strikes, which have pounded the country’s energy infrastructure as winter draws in.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Zelenskyy thanks Trump for resumed intelligence sharing after US Starlink ‘message’

articles.author: Harry Taylor and Jessica Murray
articles.description:
Interior minister says ‘the Republic will not yield’ to France’s worst protests in years
A dispatch here from Sam Jones, our reporter in Madrid, as protests have spread to Italy and Portugal
The angry protests that have convulsed Spain and France in recent weeks have spilled over to Italy and Portugal, with rioters clashing with police and setting property on fire in Milan, and a tent encampment springing up in Lisbon over the weekend.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Arrests over France protests rise to 1,800, with whole streets in Paris ‘devastated’ – Europe live

articles.author: Eromo Egbejule in Lagos
articles.description:
Style of emceeing based on high-octane, ad-libbed vocals has flourished thanks to its unique way of captivating crowds
For the 2015 freshmen cohort of the history degree programme at the University of Lagos, their classmate’s first-semester presentation was so captivating that they began calling him Toby Shang, after the 16th-century Chinese dynasty he had focused on.
His crowd engagement that day had been harnessed from his high school days as a ginger-man (energiser) in a three-man band and as a private tutor. By his final year at university, his viral catchphrases and infectious energy had resulted in a hit song, Shedibalabala. Today, he is one of the self-acclaimed “evangelists and pioneers” in the Afrobeats sub-genre some are now calling Afrohype or lamba.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hilarious quips and ‘100,000-volt’ energy: the hypemen (and women) redefining Afrobeats music

articles.author: Chris Osuh Community affairs correspondent
articles.description:
A girl called Àìná was captured by an African king and later taken to England to become Sarah Forbes Bonetta, protege of the imperial monarch 
When she was seven years old, Bayo Randle’s great-great-grandmother Sarah Forbes Bonetta was presented to Queen Victoria at Windsor Castle as a “diplomatic gift” from an African king.
Victoria would go on to pay for Bonetta’s education, approve her marriage to one of west Africa’s wealthiest men, and become godmother to her eldest daughter.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: An extraordinary life: descendant welcomes biography of woman ‘gifted’ to Queen Victoria

articles.author: Daniel Boffey in Port Stanley, Falkland Islands; photographs and video by Sean Smith
articles.description:
Facing a slump in the polls, Argentina’s president is making economic attacks on the islands’ oil industry, and suggesting its key fisheries industry could be next 
A dozen local people and a uniformed military police officer (“Do you mind if I sit in?”) took their seats at the back of the handsome wood-panelled courtroom that doubles as the Falkland Islands’ legislative assembly. Outside, it was a typically blowy early evening. It may nominally be spring in the south Atlantic, but Stanley harbour, with its dark grey water speckled with historical shipwrecks, was a cauldron of swells and churn.
Six of the assembly’s eight members – five men, one woman – waited patiently at a row of desks and microphones. The heating had been turned up to just short of uncomfortable. Behind them, a portrait of King Charles. From the other walls, dusty photographs of governors peered down on the scene.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘4,000 people minding our own business’: four decades on, Falklands again face a hostile Argentina

articles.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Taybeh
articles.description:
French mayor and archbishop also attacked during violent attempt to stop Palestinians harvesting olives 
Israeli settler militants have attacked European diplomats, a French mayor and the archbishop of Cambrai in Taybeh, in the occupied West Bank, injuring three people and damaging a car, in the latest violent attempt to prevent Palestinians from harvesting olives on their own land.
Bernard Baudoux, mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries, was wearing his red, white and blue sash of office and attempting to enter a vehicle with diplomatic plates when he was assaulted and knocked to the ground on Saturday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats in West Bank

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
United Arab Emirates will reportedly resume payments to Yemeni forces as gains by Iran-backed Houthi fighters alarm Gulf state rulers

Yemen civil war: what sparked latest escalation and who is involved?

The United Arab Emirates has agreed to re-enter the Yemen conflict by resuming payments to some government forces fighting Iran-aligned Houthis in the south, according to sources in Yemen. In return, Saudi Arabia has agreed to provide air cover for the anti-Houthi force.
The new cooperation agreement is the first tangible sign that the deep rift between the UAE and Saudi Arabia over Yemen’s future is starting to be healed – if only because the advance by Houthi forces across Yemen has alarmed all the rival Gulf state rulers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UAE agrees with Saudi Arabia to re-enter Yemen conflict amid Houthi gains

articles.author: Kat Wong with agencies
articles.description:
Australian ​brothers Jake ​and Callum Robinson, and ​their ‌American friend Carter Rhoad, were killed while on a surf trip in Baja California in 2024

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Mexican ⁠judge ⁠has sentenced ​three men to 158 years ⁠and nine months in prison each for ⁠the murder of ​two Australian ‌brothers ‌and their American friend during ‌a 2024 surf trip to the state of Baja California.
The ‌defendants were declared guilty a week ​ago of homicide, aggravated robbery, robbery with violence and vehicle theft ⁠with violence, crimes committed against ​Australian ​brothers Jake ​and Callum Robinson, and ​their ‌American friend ​Carter Rhoad.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mexican judge sentences three men to 158 years in prison for murders of Australian and US surfers​

articles.author: Jonathan Watts
articles.description:
Forest clearance at smallest total since records began in 1988 in success for Lula ahead of presidential run-off
Deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon has fallen to its lowest level since records began, new government data shows.
But whether this globally important success is maintained or reversed is on a knife edge ahead of a presidential election run-off on 25 October between two candidates with sharply different visions for the future of the rainforest and how that affects relations with the US under Donald Trump.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brazilian Amazon deforestation falls to lowest on record as pivotal vote looms

articles.author: Rowena Mason, Lisa O’Carroll and Jasper Jolly
articles.description:
Beijing warns against ‘discriminatory’ step after France drops opposition to British role in Made in Europe package
No 10 has left the door open to imposing tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles as part of the Made in Europe package, prompting a warning from Beijing that such a move would be “discriminatory”.
Downing Street said on Friday that it would “welcome the objective to have the UK included in the Industrial Accelerator Act” after France dropped its opposition to Britain joining the scheme.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No 10 leaves option open to impose Chinese EV tariffs if UK joins EU scheme

articles.author: Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Lula reverses position on age of responsibility for ‘heinous’ crimes in what many see as a desperate electoral gambit
Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has announced that he now supports lowering the age of criminal responsibility for “heinous” crimes from 18 to 16, reversing a longstanding policy in what is widely seen as a desperate electoral gambit.
The U-turn, which Lula announced during a Thursday night interview with TV Globo, comes with the presidential runoff in just over a week. The incumbent faces an uphill battle to overturn the first-round victory of his opponent, the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who remains slightly ahead at the polls.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brazil’s Lula says he now backs lowering age of criminal responsibility to 16

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Abhijeet Dipke was detained before planned anti-government demonstrations in Delhi
The leader of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) youth movement, Abhijeet Dipke, was detained by police on Friday and then later formally arrested as authorities cracked down on fresh anti-government protests in the Indian capital.
Dipke was detained before a planned Friday evening demonstration he had called in central Delhi, urging supporters of the movement to come out and hold up the Indian flag.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s Cockroach Janta party leader arrested amid crackdown on protests

articles.author: Matt Andrews and Ed Walton for MetDesk
articles.description:
Landslide blocks river and triggers downstream flooding, while summer temperatures persist in Portugal
Flash floods have swept through Nepal’s central Gorkha district after a pre-dawn landslide on 11 October blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, triggering severe downstream flooding. Two villages in the worst-affected Chumanubri rural municipality were reportedly destroyed, with homes, roads and bridges washed away. Part of a hydropower station was also damaged.
After river levels surged from 2 metres to nearly 8.5 metres within hours, the national disaster risk reduction and management authority reported that 204 homes were damaged, and more than 650 people had been affected. More than 100 foreign trekkers were stranded in the popular hiking region. The floods come just two months after catastrophic flooding and landslides devastated parts of the country on the border with Tibet, leaving thousands dead or missing.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Flash floods destroy villages in central Nepal

articles.author: Oliver Holmes
articles.description:
Images from New Zealand aerial survey of Nikumaroro in 1938 offer new clues over aviator’s disappearance
A New Zealand museum has released nearly 50 photos from a 1938 aerial survey of the island where Amelia Earhart is believed to have crash-landed, offering amateur sleuths new evidence to scour for traces of the pioneering aviator and her plane.
The black-and-white images were published by the Air Force Museum of New Zealand after renewed interest in one of the biggest mysteries of the 20th century, spurred by a US expedition to the Pacific atoll of Nikumaroro in search of new clues.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Museum releases historical photos of island where Amelia Earhart may have crashed

articles.author: Stefano Valentino in Sulawesi and Ajit Niranjan
articles.description:
Mines in supply chains of western carmakers linked to widespread deforestation of primary rainforest in nickel-rich lands inhabited by Tolaki people in Indonesia
Volkswagen, Ford and Tesla are among the electric carmakers whose batteries may contain nickel mined in indigenous woodlands plagued by deforestation, an analysis has found, highlighting the struggle to make vehicles that are free from environmental destruction.
Corporate disclosures and trade flows from the last two years show mines in the battery supply chains of automotive giants are linked to the loss of trees in Sulawesi, a wildlife hotspot in Indonesia that houses the world’s largest nickel deposits. The metal is widely used in cathodes in car batteries because it boosts energy density and increases range.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Revealed: VW, Ford and Tesla batteries linked to destructive deforestation of indigenous lands

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff
articles.description:
Chip makers and tech investors such as Samsung and SoftBank plunge as potential interest rate hikes spook markets

Business news – live updates

Larry Elliott: the global economy is muddling through. But a storm is coming

An accelerating sell-off of AI-linked shares has hit global markets, as fears over rising inflation and future interest rate hikes spooked traders already wary of the heavily indebted sector.
South Korea’s benchmark Kospi 200 index, which is heavily skewed towards the companies that make memory chips, fell more than 8% overnight to a six-month closing low, triggering circuit breakers that brought trading to a halt at various points.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tech market sell-off deepens amid fears over US inflation and AI debt

articles.author: Reuters in Islamabad
articles.description:
Another three pupils from al-Khair school in Peshawar in critical condition after search for survivors
At least 34 schoolchildren and a female teacher have died after the roof of a school collapsed during morning classes in the northern Pakistani city ⁠of Peshawar.
As panicked parents ​and relatives thronged the site of the privately run al-Khair school to search for their loved ones, rescue workers spent hours pulling children from the rubble.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistan school roof collapse kills at least 34 children and teacher

articles.author: Sarah Johnson
articles.description:
At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reports
Mass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a new report.
More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February, according to HIV Justice Network, an organisation quoted in the Human Rights Watch (HRW) report. Among these, at least 84 were charged with “voluntary HIV transmission”, solely on the basis of their HIV status.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested

articles.author: Kate Lamb and agencies
articles.description:
Having tried cloud seeding and water bombing, one pilot project will see dry ice dispersed by plane across the province of South Sumatra
As fires ravage Indonesia, emitting a toxic smoke that has drawn the ire of regional neighbours, the government is testing an unusual new approach to tackle the haze: dry ice.
Having tried cloud seeding, water bombing and sending in army personnel to fight the fires, Indonesia’s coordinating security minister said dry ice would be dropped on the province of South Sumatra on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indonesia fights fire with dry ice as toxic haze spreads across region

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
Article in Atlantic claims The Blue Fighter was artificially generated, days after it won Caine prize for African writers
The Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied using AI to write a prize-winning short story after an article in the Atlantic said software had flagged it as almost completely AI-generated.
Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter was announced as the winner of the prestigious Caine prize for African writers on 6 October. Five days later, The Atlantic published an article by the author and journalist Vauhini Vara titled: “Yet Another Literary prize winner Seems to Be AI.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza denies using AI to write prize-winning story

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Hannah Ellis-Petersen; produced by Angus Neale; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin; executive producer Zoe Hitch
articles.description:
A fresh wave of protests by India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has been met with a brutal crackdown by Narendra Modi’s government and the closure of a historic protest site in Delhi. Two of the movement’s leaders have been imprisoned for five days for violating suppression measures. The protests, which began over frustration about education and unemployment, are now focused on voting rights. Modi’s government denies claims it is seeking to disenfranchise millions of voters. But its treatment of protesters has been criticised by the UN and Amnesty International and raised concerns that India is sliding further into autocracy. Lucy Hough speaks to South Asia correspondent Hannah Ellis-Petersen – watch on YouTube
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s cockroach protesters defy Modi’s crackdown – The Latest

articles.author: Melody Schreiber
articles.description:
Health minister says government ‘did not authorize’ Danish-led hepatitis B trial in babies backed by RFK Jr
Guinea-Bissau has not approved the controversial hepatitis B study in newborns that would be funded by the US government and private partners, the African country’s minister of health said on Tuesday.
The study, which would not investigate the safety or effectiveness of vaccines but would instead track “nonspecific” health outcomes like overall mortality or neurodevelopmental conditions, has been championed by Robert F Kennedy Jr, secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime anti-vaccine activist.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Guinea-Bissau denies it has approved controversial vaccine trial in newborns

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das will spend spend five days in prison for entering Delhi’s Jantar Mantar – a historic protest site that has been closed by authorities

Why Indian voters are on the streets

Two leaders of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement have been sent to jail for five days for violating a ban on protests at a site in central Delhi.
A court ordered that Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, leaders of the Cockroach Janata party (CJP) movement, spend five days in Delhi’s Tihar prison for jumping over police barricades, holding up slogans and waving the Indian flag at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Leaders of India’s Cockroach party jailed for violating ban on protest site

articles.author: Sanya Mansoor
articles.description:
‘Meta owes us an explanation,’ group says as organizers fear censorship after account goes dark for several hours
The coalition leaders behind nationwide pro-democracy protests that have drawn millions of Americans to the streets in recent years were frustrated when its Instagram account was temporarily shut down during its latest demonstration on Saturday.
The No Kings movement’s account went dark for several hours while protests focused on increasing early voter turnout were underway, sparking censorship fears.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Outrage after Meta suspends No Kings Instagram account during protests

articles.author: José Olivares and Sanya Mansoor in New York
articles.description:
Ex-president urges Americans to defend congresswoman, saying ‘there’s no reason to believe it will stop with her’
Former US president Barack Obama condemned comments by Donald Trump’s “border czar” that the Republican presidential administration could “of course” strip Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar of her citizenship and deport her.
Obama wrote Sunday morning, on X, that “the full weight of the federal government is being brought down on a law-abiding elected official because she has dared to criticize the president.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Obama condemns comments by ‘border czar’ that Ilhan Omar could ‘of course’ be denaturalized

articles.author: Sanya Mansoor and agencies
articles.description:
Judge orders government to notify her by 8pm ET Sunday whether its position changed from Friday’s court filing 
Donald Trump posted on Truth Social on Sunday that “restoration work will begin” on 15 November to a historic public golf course in Washington DC despite a federal judge’s court order to pause his plans over environmental and historic preservation concerns.
US district judge Ana Reyes had ruled earlier this year that the federal government must give notice before any substantive construction work on the East Potomac golf course could proceed, and last week issued an order halting the removal of trees at the site, which she called “inexcusable”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump plans to begin DC golf course renovation in defiance of judge’s order

articles.author: Maya Yang
articles.description:
Jan Crawford had praised man who asked Democratic candidate whether he would disavow Muslim Brotherhood
CBS’s chief legal correspondent Jan Crawford has apologized for and deleted a social media post praising a man who questioned Democratic Michigan US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed about the Muslim Brotherhood during a town hall on Saturday.
On Sunday, Crawford, who initially joined CBS in 2009, wrote on X: “Earlier, I tweeted a video from an Abdul El-Sayed town hall. I deleted that tweet because it was a violation of CBS News standards. I apologize.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: CBS reporter apologizes and deletes post praising Abdul El-Sayed heckler

articles.author: Sam Levine in New York
articles.description:
From the attorney general stumping for Republican candidates to federal agents raiding the home of a Democratic congresswoman up for re-election, the department is violating longstanding norms
Donald Trump’s justice department has aggressively inserted itself into the midterm elections in the contest’s final weeks, shattering the department’s longstanding practice of political neutrality and leaving little doubt about the department’s willingness to help should the president attempt to subvert elections where his party is forecasted to lose seats and ultimately control of Congress.
In the last few weeks, federal agents have raided the home of a Democratic congresswoman up for re-election. It has touted criminal charges and arrests of non-citizens charged with voter fraud. The attorney general has hit the campaign trail to stump for Republican candidates. And the department gave California election officials 48 hours to investigate the citizenship of 20,000 people, and then sued the state when it refused to comply. The FBI also recently published a video criticizing Michigan senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and other Democrats, drawing an immediate rebuke from one watchdog, who said the video “has no place in a democratic society”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Trump’s justice department is shattering practice of political neutrality as midterms loom

articles.author: Nicola Jennings
articles.description: Continue reading...
articles.title: Nicola Jennings on Trump’s new White House press secretary – cartoon

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
Protesters held rallies across the US as part of the 'No Kings' movement, voicing opposition to the Trump administration and calling for early voting ahead of November's midterm elections. The rallies coincide with heightened legal battles surrounding voting rules, including a recent federal lawsuit filed against California regarding mail-in ballots and warnings from the justice department concerning ballot processing. Current opinion polls suggest Democrats will win the House of Representatives in the upcoming midterms, while the Senate remains too close to call
 Continue reading...
articles.title: 'No Kings' protesters rally across the US – video

articles.author: Gene Marks
articles.description:
Overall, economic sentiment for Trump is poor, but small businesses seem fairly confident, according to several surveys
There are 34m small businesses in the United States. They employ approximately half of the country’s workers and generate about half of the country’s GDP. They’re an important voting block. So how are they feeling about the economy as we head into November’s midterm elections? Overall, economic sentiment for Donald Trump is poor but small business – admittedly a diverse demographic that’s hard to poll – seems fairly confident. A number of recently published surveys and reports can help understand their mood.
Confidence is generally stable.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Small business owners are doing OK – but will that help Trump overcome his low approval ratings?

articles.author: Dave Schilling
articles.description:
In attempting to turn a public space in DC into an enclave for elites, Trump is moving the US capital closer to Graceland

When is a tree not a tree? When it’s an obstacle to a par-3. If a tree falls in the middle of a golf course, does it make a sound? Yeah, probably. I wasn’t there, but I have to assume, based on my limited knowledge of the laws of physics.
What I do know is that Donald Trump’s crusade to clear more than 400 trees for the purposes of redeveloping East Potomac Golf Links into a championship-level course isn’t happening. For now.
Dave Schilling is a Los Angeles-based writer and humorist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: If Trump fells 430 trees in the middle of a golf course, do they make a sound?

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
Katie Zacharia, the new White House press secretary, has been fired from her role after just five days. Moments before the firing, Donald Trump told reporters he would suggest Zacharia to 'reconsider' the job, following days of intense media scrutiny around her legal credentials

Katie Zacharia fired after five days as White House press secretary

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says he will advise Katie Zacharia to reconsider shortly before she was fired - video

articles.author: Jonathan Freedland
articles.description:
The old certainties have gone. We will have to spend whatever it takes to protect ourselves in this new and dangerous world
Donald Trump must find it oddly frustrating. He keeps showing the world exactly who he is, and yet the world keeps refusing to believe it. As clearly as he can, he is announcing that he is not the leader of the free world, that he is not even a reliable member of the democratic west, that he is in fact an ally of its enemies – but the west, including Britain, either doesn’t fully get the message or can’t quite bring itself to draw the obvious conclusion.
Trump had another go this week, finding multiple ways to declare that in the war between Russia and Ukraine, he is no mediator or peace broker but a partner of Vladimir Putin. In fairness to him, the US president had loudly issued that declaration within weeks of his return to the White House when, in February 2025, he delivered an on-camera dressing down of Volodymyr Zelenskyy in the Oval Office, seeking to humiliate the Ukrainian leader by telling him “you don’t have the cards”, even as JD Vance demanded their visitor show gratitude. That should have made Trump’s position sufficiently plain, but in the past few days he has all but put it up in lights.
Jonathan Freedland is a Guardian columnist
US midterms: Trump, war and America’s future
 

 On Thursday, 5 November join Jonathan Freedland, Devika Bhat, Professor Adam Smith in London and David Smith and leading US commentator Tara Setmayer live from the US to discuss the results and their implications for the future of Trump, the US and global politics.
 

 Book tickets here or at guardian.live

articles.title: Of course Trump is helping Russia in Ukraine – he’s a master of the art of betrayal | Jonathan Freedland

articles.author: Oliver Milman in Kerrville, Texas
articles.description:
Polls show that Democrats and Republicans in battleground states want to hear more from candidates about the climate crisis
Most Americans feel unease or alarm about the climate crisis and, in both red and blue states, want to know how political leaders are going to fix it. But in midterm election campaigns across the US, candidates have responded to this desire with near silence.
People in the US have this year endured a record hot summer as well as soaring costs, equating to roughly $2,000 per household, in extra energy and mortgage payments, due to the country’s dependence on a fossil fuel supply scrambled by Donald Trump’s decision to attack Iran.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US voters want more action on global heating. Why are Democrats and Republicans staying silent?

articles.author: Guardian staff
articles.description:
Late-night host discussed Trump’s falling poll numbers and concerns over his new press secretary, Katie Zacharia

Trump’s new press secretary says it’s ‘unknown’ how much she’ll deal with media

With other hosts still on holiday, Jimmy Kimmel checked in on Donald Trump’s record-low poll numbers and beleaguered new press secretary, Katie Zacharia.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jimmy Kimmel on Trump’s new press secretary: ‘attorney in the way George Santos was volleyball champion’

articles.author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland with Arwa Mahdawi , produced by Nada Smiljanic and Danielle Stephens
articles.description:
The US vice-president is following the Donald Trump playbook, attacking the Democrats, attempting to make jokes and even swearing more. Jonathan Freedland talks to Arwa Mahdawi about why Vance is making such an effort to court voters
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is JD Vance campaigning for the midterms – or 2028? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Fabiola Cineas
articles.description:
Coalition has planned more than 3,000 events on Saturday to encourage voting before election day
The coalition that has drawn millions of Americans into the streets to fight for democracy over the past two years is shifting its strategy this weekend.
On Saturday, No Kings organizers and partners will hold thousands of events across all 50 states and Washington DC to get people to the polls early for the US midterm elections. With high-stakes races that will determine control of Congress, organizers say getting out the vote before election day can ease burdens on election workers and build confidence in voters, allowing them to avoid hiccups such as long lines and potential election threats.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Too big to rig’: No Kings movement heads to the polls to boost early voting

articles.author: Karim Zidan
articles.description:
The mixed martial arts organization has had links to the US president for years. Now it could be involved in training federal agents
In the lead-up to UFC Freedom 250 – the cagefighting spectacle that took place on the South Lawn of the White House to mark Donald Trump’s 80th birthday this past summer – the FBI announced that a handful of UFC fighters would visit the bureau for an exclusive training seminar for federal agents.
Taking place at the FBI Special Agent Academy in Quantico, Virginia, the March seminar put roughly 300 federal agents and academy students through specialized hand-to-hand combat training with seven past and current UFC fighters, including former middleweight champion Chris Weidman, who was pictured giving attendees advice on warding off attackers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: From the Octagon to Quantico: UFC teaching the FBI to fight is its latest tie to Trump world

articles.author: Oliver Laughland, Tom Silverstone, Steve Glew, Ivan Kuraev and Katie Lamborn
articles.description:
As the midterm elections loom, Oliver Laughland and Tom Silverstone travel to rural West Virginia, a Republican party stronghold, to explore how soaring gas prices, war in the Middle East and datacenter expansion are affecting Donald Trump's popularity among his base. Although the state remains staunchly Republican, there are signs of a new politics emerging – and local Democrats are looking to capitalize on it
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why one of the US's reddest counties is losing faith in Trump – video

articles.author: Kiran Stacey
articles.description:
‘Sovereignty without the ability to act on it is not autonomy,’ paper by Institute for Public Policy Research says
Britain cannot deal effectively with geopolitical crises such as Russian aggression and political turmoil in the US without rejoining the EU, according to an influential thinktank.
The Institute for Public Policy Research has become the latest organisation with ties to the Labour party to call for the UK to re-enter the bloc, after Andy Burnham said he wanted to examine all possible options.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Britain cannot deal effectively with geopolitical crises without rejoining EU, says thinktank

articles.author: Jasper Jolly
articles.description:
Premium paid over French counterparts has risen to almost £30 a megawatt hour, analysis by lobby group finds
British steelmakers have been pushed further behind European rivals on electricity costs after the US-Israeli war on Iran caused a surge in global gas prices.
The premium paid by the British industry over its French counterpart has risen to almost £30 a megawatt hour (MWh), its highest level in three years, according to analysis by the lobby group UK Steel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Electricity costs put UK steelmakers in worst position in three years against EU rivals

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Passengers urged to ‘share the carriage, not the noise’ as guidance sets out £100 penalties for nuisance behaviour
Andy Burnham has announced a crackdown on “headphone dodgers” who play loud music on public transport, as he extends his promise to give voters “breathing space” in the confines of a train carriage.
The prime minister will unveil a campaign against nuisance behaviour on public transport on Monday, alongside guidance allowing local transport authorities to levy fines of up to £100 for non-compliance.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham launches campaign against ‘headphone dodgers’ on public transport

articles.author: Hanad Ahmed
articles.description:
Antibody patterns in the blood may help doctors identify people at risk so they can be treated earlier, research shows
Patterns of antibodies in people’s blood could predict the onset of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) a decade before diagnosis, according to research that raises hopes for catching the condition early.
Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis, the two main forms of IBD, are typically treated only after symptoms appear, when the gut has already been damaged. But scientists found that the immune system sends warning signals up to a decade before diagnosis, paving the way for potentially earlier detection and even prevention.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Warning signs could predict inflammatory bowel disease a decade before diagnosis

articles.author: Anna Bawden and Kiran Stacey
articles.description:
Exclusive: Former health secretary says upfront investment in support is needed ‘if we are going to end the Neet crisis’
Ministers should cut welfare spending to fund more employment support if it wants to end the youth Neet crisis, the author of a government-led review has said.
Alan Milburn, the Tony Blair-era health secretary, told the Guardian he believed ministers should reduce benefits payments to help pay for more employment support, opening a potentially contentious debate within the Labour party over welfare cuts.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cut benefits to fund work support for young people, says Neet review author Alan Milburn

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll senior correspondent
articles.description:
UK home secretary’s meeting comes after PM said he wanted to rejoin European law enforcement databases
The UK home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, will meet the EU’s home affairs commissioner on Monday for further talks just days after Andy Burnham said he wanted to rejoin European law enforcement databases from which the UK has been locked out of since Brexit.
According to the European Commission, they will discuss “migration, border management, law enforcement cooperation and counter-terrorism”, with the latest Frontex data published on Monday showing a 43% decline in small boats crossing the Channel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Shabana Mahmood to hold talks with EU over law enforcement cooperation

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Green leader in England and Wales calls ‘debates about words’ unhelpful and denies recent motion was controversial
Zack Polanski has said Zionism in its current form is racist, that no country has a right to exist, and that the Green party motion on the issue was not controversial.
The leader of the Green party in England and Wales gave an unapologetic interview to the BBC on Sunday two weeks after his party approved a motion equating Zionism with racism.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Zack Polanski says application of Zionism is racist and no state has right to exist

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
Female colleague says she was forced out shortly after incident with Luke Campbell, Hull and East Yorkshire mayor 
A Reform UK mayor is under police investigation for allegedly showing “naked and sexualised” images of himself to a female member of staff.
Luke Campbell, a former Olympic boxing champion and the mayor of Hull and East Yorkshire, is understood to have been questioned under caution by Humberside police earlier this month.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Police investigate Reform mayor for allegedly sharing ‘naked and sexualised’ images of himself

articles.author: Dalya Alberge
articles.description:
Exclusive: Play anonymously published in 1596 was collaboration between Shakespeare and Christopher Marlowe, according to computer analysis
Dramatic new evidence concludes that the play Edward III should be added to William Shakespeare’s canon, and also that it was a major collaboration with his contemporary rival Christopher Marlowe.
The history was published anonymously in 1596, and it has long been thought that Shakespeare wrote at least a few scenes. However, Dr Rory Loughnane, a leading scholar and co-author of the research, told the Guardian that computerised textual analysis pushed the case “beyond any reasonable doubt” that the Stratford-born playwright was the principal writer.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Scholars conclude ‘beyond doubt’ that Shakespeare was main author of Edward III

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
Scrutiny committee looks into financing of Manchester Life project as PM promises ‘full transparency’
A £55m loan to Manchester City’s Abu Dhabi owner will be investigated as part of a review into a fund for housing projects while Andy Burnham was mayor.
The prime minister has faced weeks of scrutiny over his links to Manchester City’s super-rich owners after the club was found guilty of boosting its income by £900m in a nine-year breach of financial rules.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Manchester City owner’s £55m housing loan while Burnham was mayor investigated

articles.author: Jamie Grierson
articles.description:
Amid financial pressures on household and school budgets, the theatre company is expanding access with free plays 
Six young actors step into the spotlight as a reverent silence descends on the hall at City Academy in Bristol. A boy steps forward to pose a central question: “What does it mean to be young in Britain in 2026?”
Union jack flags flash across the backdrop as three girls excitedly debate a Spice Girls reunion concert, before the focus swings back to the young boy wrestling with modern British identity. He rattles off a list of familiar cultural touchstones – fish and chips, cups of tea, Butlin’s, David Attenborough, Gogglebox and the England football team, naming heroes such as Jordan Pickford and Jude Bellingham.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bristol Old Vic tackles arts ‘emergency’ by bringing the theatre into classrooms

articles.author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: rules on same-sex wards could lead to delays in care, discrimination and animosity between groups, finds internal assessment
Trans people could face delays and a greater risk of “corridor care” under new NHS England guidance that means they will no longer be able to use same-sex wards, according to an internal report.
An NHS England impact assessment, seen by the Guardian, stated that trans people may also potentially experience discrimination and this could lead to them “avoiding accessing healthcare at all”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NHS England policy for trans people could have ‘a number of adverse impacts’, report finds

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Lengthy meeting heard grumbles about ‘blue wall’ policies and ‘Ming vase’ tactics but no real rancour
As political showdowns go, this week’s gathering of Liberal Democrat MPs, billed by some as a crunch moment for Ed Davey, was a touch underwhelming. “I had expected a damp squib,” one attender put it. “It was damper than I thought.”
Far from generating a mass of opposition to Davey’s leadership, let alone a formal challenge to his position, the lengthy gathering in a Commons committee room on Tuesday evening brought a few minor grumbles, but little else.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Damp squib’: Ed Davey can breathe easy as Lib Dem leadership challenge fails to materialise

articles.author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
articles.description:
Jason Powell also backed concentration camps as Reform councillors talk of executing grooming gang members
An aspiring Reform UK MP who advocated the use of concentration camps and said “you cannot be Muslim and British” has been suspended from the party.
The activist is one of a number featured in an ITV documentary, which will be broadcast in full on Sunday night and has already resulted in fresh questions about Reform’s vetting process.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Aspiring Reform MP who said ‘you cannot be Muslim and British’ suspended

articles.author: Tim Dowling
articles.description:
They’re healthy, versatile, sustainable and available. Yet pea consumption in the UK is at a 50-year low. Here are the curries, dips, pasta dishes and even cakes that could turn all that around
It’s not good news for the pea farmers: pea consumption in the UK has fallen to a 50-year low. According to data from Defra, the average Briton ate just 37g of peas per week in 2025, down from 144g per week in 1975.
Though a classic British staple, peas are not for everybody. Apparently only 22% of gen Z associate peas with Britain at all (which is patently ridiculous: 90% of the peas we consume in the UK are grown here, while we produce about 160,000 tonnes for freezing alone each year).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: More peas, please! 17 delicious ways to devour Britain’s most brilliant vegetable

articles.author: Mark Sweney
articles.description:
Magazine group points to restructuring bill but says it ‘remains profitable in the UK for another year’
Profits at Condé Nast’s UK arm slumped by more than a third last year, according to figures published shortly after the billionaire family that owns the luxury magazine group and titles from Vogue to GQ ruled out a sale.
The publisher, which enjoyed a bumper 2024 after booking £64m in proceeds from the sale of its UK headquarters Vogue House in London, saw pre-tax profits excluding exceptional items tumble 36% from £28m that year to nearly £18m last year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Condé Nast’s UK profits drop by more than a third as sale of Vogue publisher ruled out

articles.author: Chris Osuh Community affairs correspondent
articles.description:
A girl called Àìná was captured by an African king and later taken to England to become Sarah Forbes Bonetta, protege of the imperial monarch 
When she was seven years old, Bayo Randle’s great-great-grandmother Sarah Forbes Bonetta was presented to Queen Victoria at Windsor Castle as a “diplomatic gift” from an African king.
Victoria would go on to pay for Bonetta’s education, approve her marriage to one of west Africa’s wealthiest men, and become godmother to her eldest daughter.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: An extraordinary life: descendant welcomes biography of woman ‘gifted’ to Queen Victoria

articles.author: Press Association
articles.description:
Health secretary says government has been preparing early and will spend money on ambulances and A&E upgrades
The NHS faces a more challenging winter than normal, the health secretary has warned, as she announced a £140m increase for urgent care in England.
Yvette Cooper said the money would help increase capacity, and that the NHS has been preparing since July to deal with the impact of seasonal illnesses.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Yvette Cooper pledges £140m to boost urgent care as NHS faces ‘tough’ winter

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
Healthcare professionals retrieved files belonging to 19-year old students and a caretaker killed in Nottingham attack
A total of 15 NHS staff have now been sacked after accessing medical records belonging to the victims of a 2023 Nottingham attack, a trust said.
Valdo Calocane killed two 19-year-old students, Barnaby Webber and Grace O’Malley-Kumar, and Ian Coates, a 65-year-old caretaker, and attempted to kill three other people in the city in June 2023.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fifteen NHS staff sacked after accessing medical records of Valdo Calocane victims

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
Tweet by Sarah Helm, wife of national security adviser Jonathan Powell, ‘does not meet criminal threshold’
No further action will be taken against Sarah Helm, the wife of the prime minister’s national security adviser, after she was accused of supporting the banned protest group Palestine Action.
Helm, a journalist and author who is married to Jonathan Powell, posted on X on Thursday: “God help us authors who support Palestine and Palestine Action.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No action to be taken against wife of PM’s aide over Palestine Action post

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah and agency
articles.description:
Would-be MP recorded telling undercover reporter in ITV investigation that Muslims could not be British
A would-be Reform UK MP told an undercover reporter that Muslims could not be British and asylum seekers should be put in “concentration camps”.
The comments were recorded as part of the undercover investigation by ITV that has already seen Reform accused of “appalling behaviour” and “extreme racism”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Reform candidate filmed saying asylum seekers should be put in ‘concentration camps’

articles.author: Patrick Greenfield
articles.description:
John Swinney tells party conference SNP will use ‘six-figure war chest’ to renew argument for leaving UK
John Swinney has said that the second referendum campaign for Scottish independence “has already begun”, revealing a nationwide effort to renew the argument for leaving the UK in his keynote address to the SNP party conference.
On Saturday, the Scottish first minister said the SNP would launch its “most sophisticated campaign in history” to convince Scottish voters of the benefits of independence, backed by “a six-figure war chest”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: SNP says campaign for next referendum on independence ‘has already begun’

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
School looking to sell piece of open land beloved by people in Devon town to fund refurbishments
On Saturdays throughout autumn, residents of Totnes have met at a field on the banks of the River Dart to play ballgames, fly kites or simply sit on the grass and chat.
But it hasn’t just been about having fun – this has been a “play protest” aimed at trying to save a beloved piece of open land in the historic Devon market town.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We’re not playing games’: Parents launch playground protests to fight school field sell-off

articles.author: Patrick Barkham
articles.description:
As Mark Cocker approaches a landmark for the world’s oldest column in an English-language newspaper, he is still inspired by powerful encounters with nature
In the autumn of 1987, Mark Cocker sat in a field near Norwich and watched a jay burying acorns for the long winter ahead. He described the scene in his first country diary for the Guardian. Thirty-nine years on, some of those jay-planted acorns will be mature oaks now, and Cocker is completing his 1,000th diary for the world’s oldest column in an English-language newspaper.
In his next diary, he will reflect on the changing birdlife around Flint Clough, in the Peak District, where he first marvelled at rare birds aged 12 after devouring bird books in his bedroom. As a boy, he would find cuckoo, golden plover, ring ouzel and twite, a once-common bird which is now virtually extinct in England.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: From little acorns … to his 1,000th article for the Guardian country diary

articles.author: Alex Daniel
articles.description:
In our second in a series on high-end UK manufacturing, we visit the artisans producing rich clients’ bespoke luxury cars

‘Our town is making jeans again’: meet the firm reviving jobs and skills in Wales

They are the plaything of kings, presidents and A-listers, with Rolls-Royce enthusiasts ranging from the Sultan of Brunei to Rowan Atkinson, from King Charles III to Kermit the frog.
And at the carmaker’s factory in Goodwood, West Sussex, special requests from customers get more indulgent every year. An interior lined with 3,000 iridescent feathers, or a built-in champagne cooler, or a car built in homage to its owners’ dog, have all become part of the job.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: From 3,000 feathers to pet portraits, Rolls-Royce rides high on custom craze

articles.author: Rebecca Ratcliffe
articles.description:
As a surge in beekeepers has led to increased numbers of honeybees, researchers record them pushing bumblebees and other rival species away from flowers
Honeybees are outcompeting wild pollinators for resources by aggressively bumping into them and chasing them away from flowers, research has shown.
The study, by researchers from Anglia Ruskin University, found that areas where there were higher concentrations of honeybees had fewer wild pollinators, such as bumblebees, solitary bees and hoverflies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Honeybees are barging aside wild pollinators in hunt for pollen and nectar, study finds

articles.author: Matthew Weaver
articles.description:
Owner and mechanics fear for their health and future of the Herne Hill shop with no date for fixing problem
The leafy south London neighbourhood of Herne Hill is a haven for cyclists who can often be seen lapping the local parks and refuelling at the many cafes that line the suburban streets. But there is something foul in the air of this corner of the capital – and for once it’s not the traffic fumes hitting bicycle riders.
A toxic stench thought to be caused by untreated sewage stuck in Thames Water drains has been emanating from the subterranean depths for months, most likely caused by the summer’s lack of rain.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Stinky business: south London bike shop hit by ‘unbearable’ stench from Thames Water sewer

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Data shows 2026 could be worst harvest on record, as growers suggest painting faces on vegetables instead of carving
In the lead-up to Halloween, front porches across the country feature fat, proudly carved pumpkins, lit from within by tea lights.
But this year there is likely to be a shortage due to drought, experts have warned, with the squashes much smaller than usual.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Squash down: smaller pumpkins expected this Halloween after drought in England

articles.author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Ministers considering overhaul of apprenticeship funding scheme to tackle youth jobs crisis
Employers in England are to be forced to pay more to train an older worker than a youth apprentice under plans being drawn up by the government to tackle the youth jobs crisis.
The Guardian understands ministers plan to overhaul Labour’s apprenticeship funding scheme to increase the cost of training by 25% for a worker over the age of 25 in order to encourage businesses to train young people instead.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Plan to make firms pay more to train older workers than youth apprentices in England

articles.author: Presented by Aditya Chakrabortty with Michael Gove , produced by Frankie Tobi and Luke John Smith ; the executive producers are Maz Ebtehaj, Kirsty Major and James Tindale
articles.description:
For more than three decades, Michael Gove has been a leading figure in British Conservatism. As a journalist, government minister and now editor of the Tory bible, the Spectator, he has helped shape the right even as it has moved further rightwards. In the latest episode of Radical Thinking, Gove joins Aditya Chakrabortty to discuss the future of the right, his record on Brexit and austerity, and the Spectator’s position on Islam.

Aditya’s suggested reading:

To read the fruits of Michael Gove’s dalliance with the Marxism Today gang, look up his essay in a 1998 collection called The Moderniser’s Dilemma: Radical Politics in the Age of Blair.


For a slalom ride through Michael Gove’s years in power, read The Demented Dalek by the historian Richard J Evans in the London Review of Books.


To learn more about what’s become of the British right, there’s a column by me for the Guardian.


Phil Burton-Cartledge examines why Britain's most successful political party is now failing in his book The Party’s Over: The Rise and Fall of the Conservatives from Thatcher to Sunak.

Phil also writes a very good blog on British politics, which keeps a close eye on how each party is trying to marshal a coalition of voters. Here he is on Kemi Badenoch.


Geoffrey Wheatcroft offers an entertaining short narrative in Bloody Panico!: or, Whatever Happened to The Tory Party


For more on the economics of the Cameron years, this paper examines how the Tories failed to move the UK away from being a country of renters towards a country of makers. Two of its authors will join us for a podcast later in the series.


And if you want to read how Brexit may have cost the UK 8% of GDP, read this paper based on data from the Bank of England.


Finally, on the Spectator, read Nesrine Malik’s recent column in the Guardian: Why has Britain’s oldest political magazine become such a rabid cheerleader for Islamophobia?

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why Michael Gove worries about Britishness | Radical Thinking with Aditya Chakrabortty
